svg.title: Yomika tray mark
svg.desc: The brand mark re-derived for the Windows notification area. Same rounded plate and same two-tier ink as `yomika-mark-print.svg`, but the glyph is filled instead of stroked and reduced from five elements to three: at the 16px the tray actually gives it, the print mark's 18-unit strokes land on 0.56px and the whole thing dissolves into grey mush (user report: "在小尺寸下很难看清"). Every edge here sits on a 32-unit boundary, so a 512-unit master downsamples 1:2 to the 32px tray bitmap and 1:32 to a 16px render on exact pixel boundaries — the 128-unit stroke is a full 4px, the dot 5px across. The glyph's own box is a 384-unit square (64 to 448 on both axes), so the plate keeps the same 64 units on all four sides instead of the 88 the earlier dot left on the right. The dot's box ends on those same 448 lines and starts 96 units off the spine and the arm, so its tangents land on the grid too rather than blurring over half a pixel. The accent frame is dropped, not forgotten: at 16px it stole the width the glyph needs (candidate "C-framed" in the tray-icon study), and the plate already carries the identity.
